items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: ALL THREE memory makers now have BESI hybrid bonders evaluating HBM stacking

set.signal: CEO: all three memory makers now have BESI hybrid bonders to evaluate and define the adoption of hybrid bonding for HBM stacking - repeat orders from a memory customer for HBM applications; a Korean customer that started a lab program two years ago has moved it to the forefront, with two applications (logic and HBM stacking); 2 evaluation tools shipped to the third memory maker (a full tool-of-record evaluation, the CEO confirmed). All three are evaluating for 'one specific end customer' that 'has invited all three to have these hybrid bonded stacks available by the end of 2026 to be used in end market applications in 2027'. Timeline: 2026 is 'a major qualification year' (the first customer aiming at June/July, the second 'end of Q3, Q4'), production capabilities set up towards the end of the year for mainstream volume production in 2027. The CEO said the rule of thumb of 150 hybrid bonding systems for logic implying an HBM TAM of 600 'still stands' (a processor carries 3 or 4 memory stacks; a stack of 16 dies needs 16 bonds versus one logic device). For HBM he expects integrated lines (with Applied Materials' Kinex) rather than standalone, because HBM is dedicated high-volume production; the bonder's value to BESI is the same standalone or integrated. A possible relaxation of the JEDEC thickness standards 'does not change the advantage of using a hybrid process over a reflow process' (only one of the three needs that height). Yields: a process must be 'well up into the 99.9%'; logic hybrid bonding yields are 'very well up in the 99.99%', for HBM stacking 'one still has to prove that'.
set.figure: All 3 memory makers evaluating; HBM HB TAM 600 bonders (rule of thumb); mainstream volume production 2027

items.reason: Full text: 'HBM4E is the insertion point' is the analyst's question, not confirmed by the CEO; the repeat-order customer is not identified as the US one; the Korean customer is not identified as Samsung (the Samsung website remark is separate); the 775/825/900 micron and 20-high figures are the analyst's.
items.evidence: On the memory front, adding the third one, we now have all three who have our hybrid bonders to further evaluate and define the adoption of hybrid bonding for HBM stacking.

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Q1 2026: revenue EUR 184.9M (+28.3% YoY) on high-end mobile

set.signal: Q1 2026: revenue EUR 184.9M (+28.3% YoY) on higher shipments for high-end mobile and 2.5D AI photonics and data center applications; ORDERS EUR 269.7M (more than doubled YoY, +7.7% QoQ); net income +63.8% YoY, net margin 27.9% (vs 21.9%); GM 63.5% (increased prices offset component and energy cost inflation); net cash +186.9% QoQ to EUR 103.3M on EUR 93M cash flow from operations (more than doubled YoY); EUR 14.2M of shares repurchased in Q1 (EUR 25.5M under the current 60 million buyback program). Guidance: Q2 revenue +30%-40% QoQ with GM rising to 64%-66%, opex flat to up 10% -> H1 2026 revenue +49% vs H1 2025 at the midpoint of the Q2 guidance. Market: the latest TechInsights forecast calls for 21% assembly market growth in 2026 and 75% between 2025 and 2030 - BESI expects to SIGNIFICANTLY EXCEED those rates on its advanced-packaging leadership (flip chip, multi-module die attach, hybrid bonding, next-generation TCB).

items.reason: Full text: TechInsights' 21% / 75% is 'assembly market growth', not assembly equipment; the buyback program is stated as '60 million'.
items.evidence: The latest TechInsights forecast calls for 21% assembly market growth in 2026 and 75% between 2025 and 2030.

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Hybrid-bonding LOGIC acceleration: HB unit orders MORE THAN DOUBLED QoQ

set.signal: Hybrid-bonding LOGIC acceleration: HB unit orders MORE THAN DOUBLED QoQ and exceeded the prior quarterly peak (Q2 2024) in both total units and order value. CEO: the Taiwan customer's order scheduled for installation in the first round in AP7 was pulled forward from Q2 to Q1, and the program was enlarged - the anticipated 100 bonders 'may be significantly higher', plus orders placed for co-packaged optics. Adopters named by the CEO: AMD (the first, several families), Broadcom, the Apple M5, and roadmaps from 'another very big customer in the data center modules'; HB adoption now 20 customers (18 a quarter ago). TCB Next: 2 new orders, adoption at six customers. US: the big round for the initial HB capacity was received about 1.5 years ago and is being filled in, qualified and tested - more bonders depend on that customer's adoption. Intel EMIB: BESI has been involved 'since the very beginning in placement of these EMIB modules' and delivered the systems for Intel's significant installed capacity; rising EMIB demand 'could be a positive business impact, but as things with Intel develop as they do, we first need to see more evidence'.

items.reason: Full text: the initial US HB capacity round was 'received' (ordered) about 1.5 years ago, not delivered, and is not called a logic customer; the EMIB remark carries the CEO's hedge.
items.evidence: remember we had a big round for the initial capacity for hybrid bonding received already about 1.5 years ago. That capacity is being filled in, is being qualified, is being tested

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: The 2028 game changer: the biggest GPU vendor's next-generation GPU (2028)

set.signal: CEO, asked about the biggest GPU vendor's next-generation 3D-stacked GPU: 'that's exactly one of the major game changers, and it is forecasted to be hybrid bonding' - 'more equipment to be ordered and installed in 2027, ordered in 2026 for volume production as of 2028'. Hybrid bonder capacity: from 15 bonders theoretically per month (about 180 a year), with more floor space BESI 'can now expand that to 250 per year'; standard lead time 6 months for the 100 nanometer tool; it can satisfy any model presented by 'the big five'. Long-term model: EUR 1.5-1.9 billion revenue in the next 3-5 years (roughly 2.5-3 times current), with the field support and spare-parts infrastructure put in place. Service: 15% of revenue 'may very well move up towards the 18%, 19%, 20%' (front end typically 20%-25%, with long-term service contracts standard) as hybrid bonding follows a front-end model (close to 900 defined spare parts available within four hours, 24/7) - for gross margin 'a tailwind, certainly a tailwind'. Onshoring: the TSMC, Amkor and Micron US programs - 2026-2027 preparation and fab building, volume production as of 2028 according to those customers; BESI is engaged in those programs.
set.figure: Next-gen GPU forecast hybrid bonded (orders 2026, volume production 2028); HB capacity expandable to 250/yr; LT model EUR 1.5-1.9 billion

items.reason: Full text: 'the biggest GPU vendor ... 2028 ... 3D stacking' is the analyst's framing, now attributed as the question the CEO answered; capacity 'can now expand' to 250 per year (not already raised); the 15%-16% service share is the analyst's number - the CEO said '15%'.
items.evidence: With the increase in floor space and adjusted to a model required by several customers, we can now expand that to 250 per year.

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: China & new form factors: robust Chinese orders

set.signal: China & new form factors: several robust orders from Chinese-based customers - 2.5D CoWoS-like capacity expansion, photonics pluggables, a recovery in high-end smartphone modules; China is engaged in developing hybrid bonding, possibly in 3D stacking 'to lengthen the node size life' because it is not allowed to invest in a next generation with smaller device geometry - 'could be a very significant market', still at a very early stage; the current big China market is 2.5D mass reflow flip chip; BESI sells only what the regulations allow (US government rules, tested every six months). Capacity moving outside China: Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam (BESI's Vietnam facility is building tools, its first bonding system - not hybrid - by the end of this year, freeing Malaysia capacity for wafer-level assembly) and India (five major customers setting up production, mostly power devices). PANEL: the 310 by 310 panel is coming to market in the next year and 2 years - BESI already received orders for certain applications and its bonders can handle 310 by 310 (hybrid on panel 'a bit early'). Photonics: next-generation pluggables require more bonding steps; for the CPO process BESI 'delivered the hybrid bonding for accomplishing those kinds of contacts'.
set.figure: 310 by 310 panel orders received; China 2.5D/pluggables robust; Vietnam first bonding system by year-end

items.reason: Full text: no 'litho' and no 'mm' are stated; the Vietnam facility already builds tools - the first bonding system (not hybrid) comes by the end of the year, not the plant coming online.
items.evidence: By the end of this year, the first bonding system, not hybrid, but proxy bonding.
